observation_reviews.rationale: The recount reproduces (gicsdis2.sql on rfhcf: 1,023 / 272 / 225 / 327 / 334, 2,119.6M), but the comparison is at the wrong level, so 334 overstates the contradictions. The filer prints a GICS industry heading. gicsdis2 compares the early published sub-industry with the mode of the later published sub-industry, which is itself a mapping from that industry heading. Mapping each early sub-industry to its GICS industry (data/reference/gics_hierarchy.json) and comparing with the filer's later printed industry gives 76 of the 334 rows inside the filer's own industry and 258 rows (1,665.4M) outside it. 258 is an upper bound, since some industry spellings may differ. Example: ONE Group publishes 'Restaurants' in the ICB era; the filer later prints 'Hotels, Restaurants & Leisure', which contains Restaurants, yet the row counts as differing because the later mode label is 'Hotels, Resorts & Cruise Lines'. Equinox 'Leisure Facilities' and Lakeland 'Specialized Consumer Services' are the same case. Real cross-industry cases do exist (AthenaHealth 'Pharmaceuticals' vs printed 'Health Care Technology'; Alchemy 'Diversified Support Services' vs 'Metals & Mining'). Consequences: a detector built as proposed would false-alarm on about 23 pct of its hits, and carrying the later label back (REQ-rfhc-1 option b) would replace at least 76 finer, consistent labels with a coarser and sometimes wrong one. Required: restate at GICS industry level and propose the detector on that basis.
